newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PACKERS ROMP PAST NINERS 35-14.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PACKERS ROMP PAST NINERS 35-14.

text.p: Edgar Bennett
rushed for two touchdowns and Desmond Howard returned a punt
71 yards for a score in the Green Bay Packers' 35-14 rout of
the San Francisco 49ers in an NFC playoff game on Saturday.
The Packers also forced five turnovers in the rain at
Lambeau Field before 60,787 fans.
The 49ers played most of the game without star quarterback
Steve Young, who was hampered by bruised ribs and replaced by
Elvis Grbac early in the first quarter. Niners star receiver
Jerry Rice was held to five catches for 36 yards.
Grbac completed 19-of-36 passes for 125 yards and a
touchdown and ran for a score, but was intercepted three
times.
Green Bay advanced to the NFC Championship game for the
second straight year and will meet the winner of the
Dallas-Carolina game next Sunday in Green Bay. The Packers
have won 17 straight and 27 of their last 28 games at Lambeau.
The Packers jumped to a 21-0 lead in the first half, on
the strength of Howard's dazzling run and a hard-hitting
defence. Howard returned a punt for a touchdown 2:15 into the
game and set up another score with a 46-yard return.
"When he made our final roster," said Packers coach Mike
Holmgren, "I was hoping we had done the right thing.
Basically, we did."
Howard, who led the NFL in punt return average (15.1) in
the regular season, set the tone when he gave Green Bay the
lead before quarterback Brett Favre even touched the ball.
Howard fielded San Francisco's first punt inside the Green
Bay 30, ran up the middle, cut to his left to avert two 49ers
at midfield and raced into the end zone.
"If I can catch it cleanly we can score," said Howard. "I
made a couple of stutter steps and got past the first wave and
then the guys wiped them out for me and it was off to the
races."
Howard returned another punt 46 yards to the San Francisco
seven later in the quarter. Two plays later, Favre hit Andre
Rison with a four-yard touchdown pass with 6:16 left in the
quarter.
Favre attempted just 15 passes for the game, completing 11
for 79 yards.
"The conditions were awful," Favre said. "It was cold,
rainy and windy, which made it hard to hold onto the ball. I
think we handled it pretty well."
Green Bay's defence set up a touchdown in the second
quarter when defensive end Sean Jones recovered a fumble by
teammate Craig Newsome after an interception at the San
Francisco 14. Two plays later, Bennett scored on a two-yard
run to increase Green Bay's lead to 21-0 with 3:18 left in the
half.
Bennett finished with 80 yards on 17 carries.
The Packers were breezing along before the 49ers
capitalised on two Green Bay miscues late in the first half
and early in the second half to set up two touchdowns.
A punt bounced off the foot of Chris Hayes and was
recovered by San Francisco's Curtis Buckley at the Green Bay
26 in the second quarter. Five plays later, Grbac hit Terry
Kirby with an eight-yard touchdown pass with 24 seconds left
in the half to put San Francisco on the board.
The 49ers then struck quickly in the second half after
Green Bay's Don Beebe misplayed the opening kickoff and San
Francisco recovered the ball. Grbac eventually scored on a
two-yard bootleg run.
Green Bay responded with a 12-play, 72-yard touchdown
drive which consumed nearly eight minutes.
Young, who started the game with a flak jacket to protect
his ribs, was able to play only two offensive series' in the
first quarter.
"I couldn't lift my arm to throw," said Young, who took
novocaine shots before the game to numb the pain. He completed
just 2-of-5 passes for eight yards.
"I couldn't breathe right and my right hand seemed numb at
times. I got a painkiller, and I wanted to try, but...."
San Francisco also lost Pro Bowl defensive tackle Bryant
Young late in the first quarter, after apparently suffering a
a back and neck injury. X-rays were negative.
